title: Unary Normalization Preserves Runs
statement: Let $M$ be a finite deterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be a binary input, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$, and let $t\in\mathbb{N}$. Reinterpreting the configuration reached after $t$ steps of the input-normalized machine from $c$ on the all-ones input of length $|x|$ gives exactly the configuration reached after $t$ steps of $M$ from the unary reinterpretation of $c$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite deterministic machine over the binary alphabet
A configuration of the machine on $x$
replaced: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine over the binary alphabet, $d$ a configuration on an input $x$, and $t$ a step count. The unary reinterpretation of the $t$-step run of the input-normalized variant of $M$ from $d$ equals the $t$-step run of $M$ from the reinterpretation of $d$.
